slides.title: Composite solids: ==one piece at a time==

slides.stem: A grain silo consists of a cylinder with radius $5$ meters and height $12$ meters, topped by a cone with the same radius and a height of $4$ meters. What is the total volume of the silo, in cubic meters?

slides.intro: Name each solid, then add the volumes.
slides.trapWhy: $400\pi$ treats the cone like a cylinder.

slides.title: Cones and pyramids carry a third
slides.body:
Composite volume is a sum of named pieces. Compute each with its own formula, then add.

The $\frac{1}{3}$ on cones and pyramids is the most-forgotten constant in SAT geometry.
